### Import packages and database 
Import a database on social media usage and assign appropriate column types. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
SM_use <- read_csv("C:/Users/kierr/Downloads/Social_media_impact_on_life.csv", 
    col_types = cols(Age = col_number(), 
        Daily_Usage_Hours = col_number(), 
        Weekend_Extra_Hours = col_number(), 
        Sleep_Duration_Hours = col_number(), 
        Sleep_Quality_Score = col_number(), 
        Late_Night_Usage = col_character(), 
        Perceived_Stress_Score = col_number(), 
        Mental_Health_Index = col_number(), 
        Academic_Performance_GPA = col_number()))

View(SM_use)

```

### Describe a categorical variable
In this study's sample, Instagram was the most reported primary platform followed by TikTok and YouTube, with each platform having over 750 respondents that reported it as their primary social media app. Snapchat, Reddit, Twitter, and LinkedIn each had under 500 respondents report it as their primary platform. Values were similar among different platforms. 

```{r}
SM_use_platform <- SM_use %>%
  group_by(Primary_Platform) %>%
  summarise(Primary_Platform_Count = n())

SM_use_platform

SM_use_platform_graph <- SM_use %>%
  ggplot() +
    geom_bar(mapping=aes(x = Primary_Platform))

SM_use_platform_graph

```

### Describe a continuous variable
Daily social media usage in this dataset has a skewed distribution. Due to this I reported a 5 number summary instead of the mean and standard distribution. Social media usage ranged from 0.9 to 14 hours per day with a median of 4.7 hours. 

```{r}
SM_use_daily_usage_graph <- SM_use %>%
  ggplot() +
    geom_histogram(
      mapping = aes(x = Daily_Usage_Hours),
      bins = 30
    )

SM_use_daily_usage_graph

SM_use_daily_usage_descriptive_stats <- SM_use %>%
  summarise(
    min_use = min(Daily_Usage_Hours),
    q1_use = quantile(Daily_Usage_Hours, probs = 0.25),
    med_use = median(Daily_Usage_Hours),
    q2_use = quantile(Daily_Usage_Hours, probs = 0.75),
    max_use = max(Daily_Usage_Hours)
  )

SM_use_daily_usage_descriptive_stats_byplatform <- SM_use %>%
  group_by(Primary_Platform) %>%
  summarise(
    min_use = min(Daily_Usage_Hours),
    q1_use = quantile(Daily_Usage_Hours, probs = 0.25),
    med_use = median(Daily_Usage_Hours),
    q2_use = quantile(Daily_Usage_Hours, probs = 0.75),
    max_use = max(Daily_Usage_Hours)
  )

SM_use_daily_usage_descriptive_stats
SM_use_daily_usage_descriptive_stats_byplatform

```

### Relationship between two variables
In this dataset individuals with higher daily usage hours tended to have a lower mental health index score, which is used to represent worse mental health. I also assigned each data point a color based on the primary platform used. No single platform appears to cluster in any particular region of the graph. 

```{r}
SM_use_usage_by_MHI_graph <- SM_use %>%
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(mapping=aes(x=Daily_Usage_Hours, y=Mental_Health_Index, color=Primary_Platform))

SM_use_usage_by_MHI_graph 
```
